One fix for "Limits in Claude Code", the key form added in v0.17.0. If you turned that switch on, upgrade.

## Changes

- **Claude Code's quota question is answered by Fusebox.**
  - With a key in the gateway form, Claude Code asks how the user stands with their limits each time it starts interactively: one message, "quota", for one token, read only for the limit headers.
  - v0.17.0 sent that message on. It carries no Claude Code prompt, so Anthropic refuses it on a subscription with a bare 429, on every account tried. Each refusal paused the model on that account for 30 seconds, doubling on repeats. A few starts in a row could pause a model on every Claude account.
  - Fusebox now answers it itself and sends it to no account: `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: allowed` while an account can take the model, else what a request would be told, with the limit and its reset when a spent subscription is the wait.
  - Only for a key in the gateway form. With a plain key Claude Code never asks, and the same words from another client are a request like any other.

## Upgrading

- **Database.** No change; the usage database stays on schema 5.
- **No new settings**, and no price changes.
- **API changes:** `POST /v1/messages` with a key in the gateway form, `max_tokens: 1`, no tools, no streaming and the single user message "quota" is answered by Fusebox: a 200 with an empty message, or the pool's own error. It is not recorded as a request.

## Known issue

- **SQLite advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0459 ([#60](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/issues/60)).** Unchanged from v0.17.0.

Validation: 1,044 Rust tests (13 ignored), 193 dashboard tests and 59 Python tests passed, with formatting and Clippy; the Release workflow tests the tag on Linux, macOS and Windows. The dependency audit still fails only on the advisory above. Tried with Claude Code 2.1.323, interactively, against a build of this fix: nothing reaches the provider at start-up, prompts are answered, and a spent limit shows as "5-hour limit reached" with its reset. The defect was seen on production under v0.17.0: two interactive starts, two rounds of three refusals.

[Full comparison with v0.17.0](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.17.0...v0.17.1).
